notes: This page is the 'Meet the Fan Designer' profile page (Mark Smiley). It has no building step, so no pieces or joins were added.
This page shows the finished model and translation links. It has no building step, so no pieces or joins were added.
This page is the generic introduction showing how to open the box and sort the pieces. It has no building step, so no pieces or joins were added.

This page assembles the minifigure (hair, head, torso with arms and hands, legs). None of these pieces are in the provided parts list or catalogue, so I added nothing. If the minifigure should be recorded, it needs part types and ids.
Step 1: the grey 1x6 plate (b2) rests on the black 6x10 base plate (b1), running along the long side near the back edge.
The exact stud offset (row 2, columns 3-8) is estimated from the illustration. Only b1 and b2 are certain.
Ids b1 and b2 are new. Earlier pages added no pieces. The minifigure on page 5 was not recorded.
Step 2: four light bluish gray 2x2 corner plates (b3-b6) are added around the edge of the black 6x10 base (b1). All four rest on b1.
The stud positions and which corner stud is empty are estimates from the small illustration. The part count (4) and type (lego-2420) are certain.

The picture suggests the grey plates form a continuous frame along the back and left edges. If so, b2 from page 6 may actually sit in the back row (row 1) rather than row 2. That earlier placement is not corrected here.
Step 3: a black 1x2 plate (b7) goes on the base (b1). A dark blue 2x3 plate (b8) is pressed onto the black plate, near the right end of the base.
Sub-step 1 builds the black 1x2 under the blue plate's end, and sub-step 2 places the blue plate on top. The assembly then goes on the right end of the base.
The exact stud positions and how far the blue plate overhangs are estimated from the illustration, so b8 is recorded as resting only on b7.
Step 4: two dark bluish gray 1x8 tiles (b9, b10) are laid side by side along the front edge of the base (rows 5 and 6), resting on the base b1.

The columns (3-10) are estimated from the illustration. They overlap with the front corner plates b5 and b6 as I guessed them in step 2. Those guesses were probably wrong, because the picture shows no grey plate at the front right.
Step 5: a yellow 1x10 brick (b11) runs along the back edge of the base. Three yellow 1x2 bricks form the side walls: b12 and b13 down the left side, b14 at the back right beside the blue plate.
The illustration shows grey plates under the full back row, so I recorded the 1x10 as resting on b3, b2 and b4. That puts b2 in the back row, and the stud coordinates I gave b2 on page 6 may be off.
Which supports sit under b12, b13 and b14 is estimated from the small illustration. The part types and counts are certain.
Step 6: a dark blue 2x2 brick (b15) goes on four studs of the dark blue 2x3 plate (b8). A flat silver grille tile (b16) covers the two remaining studs on the outer end, forming the first stair step.
Which end of b8 the tile covers is judged from the illustration.
Step 7: a second layer of yellow bricks goes on the back wall. A 1x6 brick (b19) sits on the 1x10 (b11). A 2x2 corner brick (b17) sits at the back right on b11 and b14. A 1x1 brick (b18) sits on b14.
The positions along the wall (1x6 over columns 3-8, corner over columns 9-10) are estimated from the illustration. The part types and counts are certain.
Step 8: a dark blue 1x2 brick (b20) goes on the inner half of the blue 2x2 brick (b15). A flat silver grille tile (b21) covers the outer two studs, forming the second stair step.
Which half of b15 the tile covers is judged from the illustration.

Step 9 builds the crank mechanism as a separate sub-assembly. Sub-step 1: yellow bush (b23) goes on the tan axle pin (b22). Sub-step 2: the tan pin goes into the crankshaft's offset hole (b24). Sub-step 3: the crankshaft axle goes through the yellow Technic brick (b25), and the white hub (b26) is pushed onto the crankshaft's axle end.
I couldn't tell exactly how the white hub (b26) meets the crankshaft end, because the hub has an axle and the crankshaft end is also an axle. I recorded it as a rigid join between the two axle ports.
The sub-assembly is not yet attached to the base.

Step 10 (page 15): the crank sub-assembly from the previous page is attached. Its yellow Technic brick (b25) is pressed onto the left end of the back wall, on the 1x10 brick (b11). The crankshaft end with the tan pin points into the model's interior, and the white hub (b26) sticks out the back.
No new pieces. The column position on b11 (columns 1-2) is estimated from the illustration and from the 1x6 brick (b19) placement in step 7.

Step 10: a yellow 2x2 corner brick (b27) and a yellow 1x1 brick (b28) are added on top of the left side wall, raising it to match the back wall. This is the second corner brick and second 1x1 of the set, after step 7.
Which studs of b12 and b13 they rest on is estimated from the illustration. The corner brick may also overhang or touch the neighbouring bricks.

Step 11 builds the red coin box as a separate sub-assembly. Sub-step 1: the door (b31) hinges onto the red box (b30). Sub-step 2: two coin tiles (b32, b33) go inside the box. Sub-step 3: a red grille tile (b29) goes on top of the box.
The box is not attached to the base yet.
The small top piece is shown with ridges, so I took it as the red lego-2412b grille tile rather than the red door-rail plate lego-32028.
The box lists 4 coins, but only the '2x' callout is clearly inserted. The other two (b34, b35) are shown loose beside the box, so I added them without joins. They may go in the box or stay loose.
The grille tile is on the two top studs on one side of the box, estimated from the illustration.
Step 12 (page 18): the red coin box sub-assembly from step 11 (b30 with door b31, grille tile b29 and coins) is pressed onto the base at the front left, next to the yellow side wall. No new pieces.
The exact studs (rows 3-4, columns 2-3 of b1) are estimated from the illustration, and the box may also touch the nearby tiles and walls.

Step 13 (page 19, labelled 12) is built 2x. Each copy has two yellow 1x4 plates stacked on each other (b36/b37 and b39/b40) and a yellow curved 2x4 brick (b38 and b41) pressed on top. Both copies are listed in full.

The illustration is ambiguous about how the stacked plates meet the curved brick. The stripes at the end of the brick suggest the stack is under the brick's studded row, so I recorded the brick resting on the top plate.
These are loose sub-assemblies and are not yet attached to the base.

Step 14 (page 20): the two curved yellow sub-assemblies from the previous step are attached. The one from b36-b38 goes on the left side wall, over b25, b27 and b28. The one from b39-b41 goes on the right back wall, over b17 and b18. No new pieces.
Which copy goes on which side is a judgement: the arrows are ambiguous, and either copy is physically identical.
The stud-level contacts are estimated from the illustration. The right-hand assembly's fourth stud overhangs the blue steps, so I gave it no support edge.

Step 13 (page 21): sub-step 1 pushes a tan axle pin (b43) into the pin hole of a yellow Technic brick (b42). Sub-step 2 fits a grey bush (b44) onto the pin's axle end. The assembly is then pressed onto the back wall, on the 1x6 brick (b19).
The yellow 1x4 brick in the parts box for this step is not placed on this page, so I recorded nothing for it. It will probably be added on the next page.
The grey bush is taken as lego-3713 (Technic Bush, the only single one in the inventory), not the thinner 32123b. The studs on b19 (columns 7-8) are estimated from the illustration.

Step 14 (page 22) builds a separate sub-assembly. Sub-step 1: a blue thin Technic beam (b45). Sub-step 2: a blue friction-ridge axle pin (b46) goes through one end hole. Sub-step 3: a light bluish gray half bush (b47) goes on the axle end. It is not yet attached to the model.
I assumed the pin sits in an end hole of the beam, as drawn. The grey bush is taken as lego-32123b, the thin 1/2 bush.

Step 14 (page 23): the blue beam sub-assembly from the previous page (b45 with pin b46 and bush b47) is attached. It is hooked onto the tan axle pin (b43) in the yellow Technic brick (b42) on the back wall and hangs down into the interior. No new pieces.
I recorded only the pivot at the wall as a turning join. The beam's lower end with the blue pin and bush hangs free in this view and seems to connect to something added later.
Which beam hole is used at the pivot (pin-hole.3) is estimated from the illustration.

Step 15 (page 24) builds a separate sub-assembly. Sub-step 1: a 3-long grey axle (b49, the '3' tag) goes into one arm of the dark brown angled triple connector (b48). Sub-step 2: a small connector piece (b50) is pushed onto the free end of the axle.

The first 1x piece in the parts box is drawn grey. I took it to be the white Technic Driving Ring Connector (lego-18948), the only unplaced piece that fits that shape. It could instead be a grey bush.
The parts box also shows 2x white pin connector hubs (lego-22961), but this page doesn't place them, so I added nothing for them.
Not yet attached to the model.
Step 15 sub-step 3 (page 25): two white pin connector hubs (b51, b52) go onto the other two arms of the dark brown angled connector (b48). The third arm already carries the grey axle (b49) with b50.
The finished connector is then placed in the middle of the mechanism. One hub meets the crank's tan pin end (b22) and the other meets the blue beam (b45). The grey axle (b49) points upward.
The hub-to-crank and hub-to-beam joins are my best reading of the small illustration. I couldn't tell the exact ports. The beam hole used (pin-hole.2) and the crank join (b22 axle) are estimated.
Step 16 (page 26): a light bluish gray 1x6 plate (b53) is the base of a new sub-assembly. A small inset picture shows the finished sub-assembly in the model's context.
Step 17: a yellow 1x4 brick (b54) goes on studs 2-5 of the plate, and a yellow round 1x1 brick (b55, b56) goes on each end stud.
This is a separate sub-assembly and is not yet attached to the main model.

Step 18 (page 27): three light bluish gray 1x2 bricks with side studs (b57-b59) go side by side on top of the step 17 sub-assembly, covering the two round bricks and the 1x4 brick. Their side studs face the front.
Step 19: a yellow 1x6 brick (b60) goes on top of the three grey bricks.
Which stud of the 1x4 and round bricks each grey brick covers follows from the six-stud row. It is estimated from the illustration.

Step 20 (page 28): the step 16-19 sub-assembly is turned over (rotate icon). Along its yellow 1x6 (b60) go, left to right: a yellow 1x2 plate (b61), a dark blue 1x2 jumper (b62), the dark blue 2x2 jumper (b63), a second blue 1x2 jumper (b64) and a second yellow 1x2 plate (b65). The plates sit across the 1-wide brick and overhang it on one side.
Step 21: three orange star tiles (b66-b68) go on the single studs of the three blue jumpers, and four flat silver round plates (b69-b72) go on the four studs of the two yellow plates.
The order of the pieces along the brick and the choice of which anti-stud ports of the jumpers touch b60 are judgements from the small illustration. The overhang side is not shown precisely.

The '4x' silver pieces on page 21 look like the round plates (lego-6141), since those are what the inventory has in Flat Silver with a stud. They could be the coin-print tiles instead, but those were used on page 17.

Step 22 (page 29): the control-panel sub-assembly from steps 16-21 is placed across the front opening. The star tiles face front, the yellow 1x6 (b60) is on top, and the grey plate (b53) is at the bottom. No new pieces.

Correction to my page 28 edges: the five plates (b61-b65) attach to the side studs of the three grey side-stud bricks (b57-b59), not to the top studs of b60. That is why the sub-assembly was turned over. The first six edges above give the corrected joins, and the earlier plate-to-b60 edges should be dropped. The overhang is one plate across a single side stud.

I couldn't find studs under the panel that it could clutch, because the front tiles (b9, b10) have none and the side walls are already covered. So I recorded only contact between the panel's base plate and the front tiles. The panel may also clutch the wall bricks on either side.

Step 23 (page 30): yellow tiles close the roof. A 1x8 tile (b73) covers the front row, two 2x4 tiles (b74, b75) cover the left and right curved bricks, and two 1x1 tiles (b76, b77) cover the studs of the yellow Technic brick (b42). The grey axle (b49) still sticks up through a gap in the middle.

The illustration is small and the roof is seen at an angle, so which studs each tile covers is estimated. For the 2x4 tiles I recorded only the four studs of one row, and for the 1x8 tile only its six middle studs over b60. All tile part types and counts are certain.
Step 24 (page 31): a flat silver grille tile (b78) goes on top of the dark blue 1x2 brick (b20), making the top step of the stairs.
Step 25 (page 32): a red 4x6 plate (b79) is the first piece of the rocket, a new separate sub-assembly (the inset shows the finished rocket). It has nothing under it, so no joins yet.

Step 26 (page 33): a white Technic 2x4 plate (b81) goes on the red 4x6 plate (b79), and a green 1x2 plate (b80) goes at its right end. The columns used (b81 on columns 2-5, b80 on column 6) are estimated.

Step 27: a red 2x2 plate (b82) and two red door-rail 1x2 plates (b83, b84) are added. In the illustration they stick out beyond the red plate's edges like wings and look like they are on the underside. I recorded them as pushed onto the underside (anti-studs) of b79.
The exact positions of b82, b83 and b84 under b79 are guesses. The part types and counts are certain: 1x red 3022 and 2x red 32028.

Step 28 (page 34): a red 2x4 wedge plate (b85) is added at the front left of the rocket body. It overhangs, so I recorded only contact with the red 4x6 plate (b79) and the red 2x2 plate (b82), not exact studs.
Step 29: six red inverted curved 2x1 bricks (b86-b91) form the rocket's curved roof. The last one (b91) is shown dropping onto the green plate (b80) at the right end.

The illustration doesn't show clearly where the other five roof bricks sit. I recorded three on the Technic plate (b81) and two on the side rows of b79. These placements are guesses. The part type and count of six are certain.

Step 30 (page 35): a red round 2x2 plate with axle hole (b92) goes on the front of the rocket, and four more red inverted curved 2x1 bricks (b93-b96) complete the curved roof. That makes ten curved bricks in total with the six from step 29.
Step 31: the rocket is turned over (rotate icon). A green 1x2 plate (b97), a white 2x4 wedge plate (b98) and a flat silver grille tile (b99) are added on the studs now facing up.
The pictures are too small to give stud-level joins for these pieces, so I recorded only rough contact edges to the nearest major plate. The grille tile is the fourth flat silver 2412b used.
The studded face shown after the turn-over doesn't match my earlier guess of what sits under the red 4x6 plate (b79), so the placements on this page are uncertain.

Step 32 (page 36): six white inverted 1x2 brackets (b100-b105, the whole stock of lego-99780) are pressed onto the studded face of the turned-over rocket. Three go along the front edge, with their side studs facing out. Three go along the back edge.
Which studs each bracket covers isn't legible at this size, so I gave the joins to the base plate b79 without ports. Their exact supporting pieces are uncertain.

Step 33 (page 37) fits out the rocket's cockpit area. A white 2x2 plate (b106), a white divider panel (b107) and a yellow seat (b109) go onto the studded face of the rocket. A yellow Technic brick (b108, the last of the three yellow ones) drops in at the front left, next to the first white bracket (b100).
All joins are given without ports because the small illustration doesn't show which studs are used. The seat and panel are assumed to sit on the main plate b79.
Step 34 (page 38): a light bluish gray 1x2-1x2 bracket (b110) is pressed onto the studs at the right (tail) end of the rocket, next to the white wedge plate (b98). It has side studs facing outward.
Which studs it uses isn't clear at this size, so I gave the join without ports. It is assumed to sit on the white wedge.

Step 35 (page 39): two red 2x2 plates (b111, b112) are stacked on the rocket's tail end, over the white wedge b98. Two flat silver cones (b113, b114) are fitted as rear nozzles. The bracket b110 has only one catalogue port for its side studs (stud.2), so both cones use that port, but they sit on its two side studs.
In sub-step 2 a Trans-Red round plate is added on top of each cone. The parts box lists 4x and the finished nozzles show two red rings each, so I recorded two stacked plates per cone (b115-b118).
The cones' catalogue entry has no stud port, so the plates are joined to the cones without a port. The red plates' exact studs are estimated.

Step 36 (page 40): on the stacked red 2x2 plates at the tail (b112), a light bluish gray handle plate (b119) takes the two studs on the cockpit side. A red 30° sloped brick (b120) takes the two studs on the rear side, next to the nozzles.
Which pair of studs each piece takes is estimated from the illustration.

Step 37 (page 41): the rocket is flipped upright and red curved shell pieces are added around it. Two long red curved 1x4 bricks (b121, b122, lego-10314) go along the sides over the white brackets. Four small red curved 1x2 bricks (b123-b126, lego-6091) fill in the ends and tail.
I matched the picture's '2x' piece to lego-10314 (long curved, no studs) and the '4x' piece to lego-6091. These are the only red curved parts left in the inventory that fit those counts.
The pictures don't show which studs each curved piece clutches, so joins are given without ports. The assignment of the four small pieces to specific neighbours is a guess.

Step 38 (page 42): twelve round 1x1 plates (six Trans-Dark Blue, six Trans-Green) are added to the outer side faces of the six white brackets (b100-b105), two per bracket, alternating blue and green. They form the rocket's row of portholes or lights.

The bracket's catalogue entry has one side port (anti-stud.2) standing for its two side positions, so both plates on a bracket use that port. The colour alternation is as drawn, but which of the two side positions gets which colour is arbitrary.

Step 39 (page 43): a black 3L axle pin with 2L axle (b141) is pushed into the pin hole of the yellow Technic brick (b108) at the rocket's nose. A trans-clear panel (b140) is added as the windscreen at the front of the cockpit. The last red 2x2 plate (b139) goes on the top rear.
The pictures don't show which studs the clear panel and red plate use, so those joins are given without ports. The panel is assumed to sit on b108 and the plate on the white plate b106.
The pin's free axle end sticks out the side of the nose, probably to connect to the ride mechanism later.

Step 40 (page 44) builds the rocket's nose cone as a separate sub-assembly. Sub-step 1: a dark blue round 2x2 jumper plate (b143) goes on the four studs of the dark blue 4x4x2 cone (b142). Sub-step 2: a trans-clear radar dish (b144) goes on the jumper plate's centre stud, then a flat silver round plate (b145) goes on top. Sub-step 3: a Trans-Red round plate (b146) goes on top.
The parts box shows small round pieces I could only match by colour. I took the first as the flat silver round plate (lego-6141) and the third as the last Trans-Red round plate.
The dish has no stud port in the catalogue, so b145 is joined to it without a port. The cone isn't attached to the rocket yet.

Step 41 (page 45): the nose cone sub-assembly from step 40 is attached to the front of the rocket. The axle end of the black axle pin (b141), which sticks out of the nose, goes into the cone's axle hole (b142). No new pieces.

Step 41 (page 46): the rocket's fins are added. A white tail shuttle (b149), the tall fin on top, goes on the red 2x2 plate at the rear (b139). Two dark blue flags (b147, b148) clip onto the handles of the handle plate (b119) at the tail, forming the side fins.
Both flags are shown clipping onto the bars of b119, so I used one clip port on each flag and clip.1 and clip.2 on the handle plate. Which flag takes which handle is arbitrary.
The first flag is already visible in place on the right side of the picture, and the second is shown with arrows.

Step 42 (page 47): the finished rocket is mounted on top of the ride base. The pin of the driving ring connector (b50) on the grey axle sticking up from the roof opening goes into one of the pin holes of the rocket's white Technic plate (b81). The rocket then turns freely on the crank mechanism. No new pieces.
The illustration only shows the rocket being lowered onto the base. I picked the middle pin hole (pin-hole.2) of b81 as the one used, and the link is recorded as a turning join.
The arrow on the page points at the nose cone's tip (the trans-red plate b146), probably showing the direction to hold the rocket, and adds no join.
Page 48 shows the completed model next to the minifigure. It has no building step, so nothing was added.
Page 49 shows how to use the finished model: turning the crank at the side makes the rocket rock back and forth. It has no building step, so nothing was added.
Page 52 is the back cover (starry background with the LEGO trademark notice). It has no building step, so nothing was added.
The two groups cut off from the model were the two loose coin tiles from page 17 (b34, b35). I had left them without joins because only two of the four coins are clearly inserted in the box.
The box is drawn with a stack of about three coins inside, so I took all four coins as the box's contents. They rest in the coin box (b30), which is joined to the base, like b32 and b33.
If the booklet instead means the last two coins to sit loose beside the model, they would be an unattached extra. The parts list still counts them.

The stud positions and which corner stud is empty are estimates from the small illustration. The part count (4) and type (lego-2420) are certain.

Step 3: a black 1x2 plate (b7) goes on the base (b1). A dark blue 2x3 plate (b8) is pressed onto the black plate, near the right end of the base.
Sub-step 1 builds the black 1x2 under the blue plate's end, and sub-step 2 places the blue plate on top. The assembly then goes on the right end of the base.
The exact stud positions and how far the blue plate overhangs are estimated from the illustration, so b8 is recorded as resting only on b7.
Step 4: two dark bluish gray 1x8 tiles (b9, b10) are laid side by side along the front edge of the base (rows 5 and 6), resting on the base b1.

The columns (3-10) are estimated from the illustration. They overlap with the front corner plates b5 and b6 as I guessed them in step 2. Those guesses were probably wrong, because the picture shows no grey plate at the front right.
Step 5: a yellow 1x10 brick (b11) runs along the back edge of the base. Three yellow 1x2 bricks form the side walls: b12 and b13 down the left side, b14 at the back right beside the blue plate.
The illustration shows grey plates under the full back row, so I recorded the 1x10 as resting on b3, b2 and b4. That puts b2 in the back row, and the stud coordinates I gave b2 on page 6 may be off.
Which supports sit under b12, b13 and b14 is estimated from the small illustration. The part types and counts are certain.
Step 6: a dark blue 2x2 brick (b15) goes on four studs of the dark blue 2x3 plate (b8). A flat silver grille tile (b16) covers the two remaining studs on the outer end, forming the first stair step.
Which end of b8 the tile covers is judged from the illustration.
Step 7: a second layer of yellow bricks goes on the back wall. A 1x6 brick (b19) sits on the 1x10 (b11). A 2x2 corner brick (b17) sits at the back right on b11 and b14. A 1x1 brick (b18) sits on b14.
The positions along the wall (1x6 over columns 3-8, corner over columns 9-10) are estimated from the illustration. The part types and counts are certain.
Step 8: a dark blue 1x2 brick (b20) goes on the inner half of the blue 2x2 brick (b15). A flat silver grille tile (b21) covers the outer two studs, forming the second stair step.
Which half of b15 the tile covers is judged from the illustration.

Step 9 builds the crank mechanism as a separate sub-assembly. Sub-step 1: yellow bush (b23) goes on the tan axle pin (b22). Sub-step 2: the tan pin goes into the crankshaft's offset hole (b24). Sub-step 3: the crankshaft axle goes through the yellow Technic brick (b25), and the white hub (b26) is pushed onto the crankshaft's axle end.
I couldn't tell exactly how the white hub (b26) meets the crankshaft end, because the hub has an axle and the crankshaft end is also an axle. I recorded it as a rigid join between the two axle ports.
The sub-assembly is not yet attached to the base.

Step 10 (page 15): the crank sub-assembly from the previous page is attached. Its yellow Technic brick (b25) is pressed onto the left end of the back wall, on the 1x10 brick (b11). The crankshaft end with the tan pin points into the model's interior, and the white hub (b26) sticks out the back.
No new pieces. The column position on b11 (columns 1-2) is estimated from the illustration and from the 1x6 brick (b19) placement in step 7.

Step 10: a yellow 2x2 corner brick (b27) and a yellow 1x1 brick (b28) are added on top of the left side wall, raising it to match the back wall. This is the second corner brick and second 1x1 of the set, after step 7.
Which studs of b12 and b13 they rest on is estimated from the illustration. The corner brick may also overhang or touch the neighbouring bricks.

Step 11 builds the red coin box as a separate sub-assembly. Sub-step 1: the door (b31) hinges onto the red box (b30). Sub-step 2: two coin tiles (b32, b33) go inside the box. Sub-step 3: a red grille tile (b29) goes on top of the box.
The box is not attached to the base yet.
The small top piece is shown with ridges, so I took it as the red lego-2412b grille tile rather than the red door-rail plate lego-32028.
The box lists 4 coins, but only the '2x' callout is clearly inserted. The other two (b34, b35) are shown loose beside the box, so I added them without joins. They may go in the box or stay loose.
The grille tile is on the two top studs on one side of the box, estimated from the illustration.
Step 12 (page 18): the red coin box sub-assembly from step 11 (b30 with door b31, grille tile b29 and coins) is pressed onto the base at the front left, next to the yellow side wall. No new pieces.
The exact studs (rows 3-4, columns 2-3 of b1) are estimated from the illustration, and the box may also touch the nearby tiles and walls.

Step 13 (page 19, labelled 12) is built 2x. Each copy has two yellow 1x4 plates stacked on each other (b36/b37 and b39/b40) and a yellow curved 2x4 brick (b38 and b41) pressed on top. Both copies are listed in full.

The illustration is ambiguous about how the stacked plates meet the curved brick. The stripes at the end of the brick suggest the stack is under the brick's studded row, so I recorded the brick resting on the top plate.
These are loose sub-assemblies and are not yet attached to the base.

Step 14 (page 20): the two curved yellow sub-assemblies from the previous step are attached. The one from b36-b38 goes on the left side wall, over b25, b27 and b28. The one from b39-b41 goes on the right back wall, over b17 and b18. No new pieces.
Which copy goes on which side is a judgement: the arrows are ambiguous, and either copy is physically identical.
The stud-level contacts are estimated from the illustration. The right-hand assembly's fourth stud overhangs the blue steps, so I gave it no support edge.

Step 13 (page 21): sub-step 1 pushes a tan axle pin (b43) into the pin hole of a yellow Technic brick (b42). Sub-step 2 fits a grey bush (b44) onto the pin's axle end. The assembly is then pressed onto the back wall, on the 1x6 brick (b19).
The yellow 1x4 brick in the parts box for this step is not placed on this page, so I recorded nothing for it. It will probably be added on the next page.
The grey bush is taken as lego-3713 (Technic Bush, the only single one in the inventory), not the thinner 32123b. The studs on b19 (columns 7-8) are estimated from the illustration.

Step 14 (page 22) builds a separate sub-assembly. Sub-step 1: a blue thin Technic beam (b45). Sub-step 2: a blue friction-ridge axle pin (b46) goes through one end hole. Sub-step 3: a light bluish gray half bush (b47) goes on the axle end. It is not yet attached to the model.
I assumed the pin sits in an end hole of the beam, as drawn. The grey bush is taken as lego-32123b, the thin 1/2 bush.

Step 14 (page 23): the blue beam sub-assembly from the previous page (b45 with pin b46 and bush b47) is attached. It is hooked onto the tan axle pin (b43) in the yellow Technic brick (b42) on the back wall and hangs down into the interior. No new pieces.
I recorded only the pivot at the wall as a turning join. The beam's lower end with the blue pin and bush hangs free in this view and seems to connect to something added later.
Which beam hole is used at the pivot (pin-hole.3) is estimated from the illustration.

Step 15 (page 24) builds a separate sub-assembly. Sub-step 1: a 3-long grey axle (b49, the '3' tag) goes into one arm of the dark brown angled triple connector (b48). Sub-step 2: a small connector piece (b50) is pushed onto the free end of the axle.

The first 1x piece in the parts box is drawn grey. I took it to be the white Technic Driving Ring Connector (lego-18948), the only unplaced piece that fits that shape. It could instead be a grey bush.
The parts box also shows 2x white pin connector hubs (lego-22961), but this page doesn't place them, so I added nothing for them.
Not yet attached to the model.
Step 15 sub-step 3 (page 25): two white pin connector hubs (b51, b52) go onto the other two arms of the dark brown angled connector (b48). The third arm already carries the grey axle (b49) with b50.
The finished connector is then placed in the middle of the mechanism. One hub meets the crank's tan pin end (b22) and the other meets the blue beam (b45). The grey axle (b49) points upward.
The hub-to-crank and hub-to-beam joins are my best reading of the small illustration. I couldn't tell the exact ports. The beam hole used (pin-hole.2) and the crank join (b22 axle) are estimated.
Step 16 (page 26): a light bluish gray 1x6 plate (b53) is the base of a new sub-assembly. A small inset picture shows the finished sub-assembly in the model's context.
Step 17: a yellow 1x4 brick (b54) goes on studs 2-5 of the plate, and a yellow round 1x1 brick (b55, b56) goes on each end stud.
This is a separate sub-assembly and is not yet attached to the main model.

Step 18 (page 27): three light bluish gray 1x2 bricks with side studs (b57-b59) go side by side on top of the step 17 sub-assembly, covering the two round bricks and the 1x4 brick. Their side studs face the front.
Step 19: a yellow 1x6 brick (b60) goes on top of the three grey bricks.
Which stud of the 1x4 and round bricks each grey brick covers follows from the six-stud row. It is estimated from the illustration.

Step 20 (page 28): the step 16-19 sub-assembly is turned over (rotate icon). Along its yellow 1x6 (b60) go, left to right: a yellow 1x2 plate (b61), a dark blue 1x2 jumper (b62), the dark blue 2x2 jumper (b63), a second blue 1x2 jumper (b64) and a second yellow 1x2 plate (b65). The plates sit across the 1-wide brick and overhang it on one side.
Step 21: three orange star tiles (b66-b68) go on the single studs of the three blue jumpers, and four flat silver round plates (b69-b72) go on the four studs of the two yellow plates.
The order of the pieces along the brick and the choice of which anti-stud ports of the jumpers touch b60 are judgements from the small illustration. The overhang side is not shown precisely.

The '4x' silver pieces on page 21 look like the round plates (lego-6141), since those are what the inventory has in Flat Silver with a stud. They could be the coin-print tiles instead, but those were used on page 17.

Step 22 (page 29): the control-panel sub-assembly from steps 16-21 is placed across the front opening. The star tiles face front, the yellow 1x6 (b60) is on top, and the grey plate (b53) is at the bottom. No new pieces.

Correction to my page 28 edges: the five plates (b61-b65) attach to the side studs of the three grey side-stud bricks (b57-b59), not to the top studs of b60. That is why the sub-assembly was turned over. The first six edges above give the corrected joins, and the earlier plate-to-b60 edges should be dropped. The overhang is one plate across a single side stud.

I couldn't find studs under the panel that it could clutch, because the front tiles (b9, b10) have none and the side walls are already covered. So I recorded only contact between the panel's base plate and the front tiles. The panel may also clutch the wall bricks on either side.

Step 23 (page 30): yellow tiles close the roof. A 1x8 tile (b73) covers the front row, two 2x4 tiles (b74, b75) cover the left and right curved bricks, and two 1x1 tiles (b76, b77) cover the studs of the yellow Technic brick (b42). The grey axle (b49) still sticks up through a gap in the middle.

The illustration is small and the roof is seen at an angle, so which studs each tile covers is estimated. For the 2x4 tiles I recorded only the four studs of one row, and for the 1x8 tile only its six middle studs over b60. All tile part types and counts are certain.
Step 24 (page 31): a flat silver grille tile (b78) goes on top of the dark blue 1x2 brick (b20), making the top step of the stairs.
Step 25 (page 32): a red 4x6 plate (b79) is the first piece of the rocket, a new separate sub-assembly (the inset shows the finished rocket). It has nothing under it, so no joins yet.

Step 26 (page 33): a white Technic 2x4 plate (b81) goes on the red 4x6 plate (b79), and a green 1x2 plate (b80) goes at its right end. The columns used (b81 on columns 2-5, b80 on column 6) are estimated.

Step 27: a red 2x2 plate (b82) and two red door-rail 1x2 plates (b83, b84) are added. In the illustration they stick out beyond the red plate's edges like wings and look like they are on the underside. I recorded them as pushed onto the underside (anti-studs) of b79.
The exact positions of b82, b83 and b84 under b79 are guesses. The part types and counts are certain: 1x red 3022 and 2x red 32028.

Step 28 (page 34): a red 2x4 wedge plate (b85) is added at the front left of the rocket body. It overhangs, so I recorded only contact with the red 4x6 plate (b79) and the red 2x2 plate (b82), not exact studs.
Step 29: six red inverted curved 2x1 bricks (b86-b91) form the rocket's curved roof. The last one (b91) is shown dropping onto the green plate (b80) at the right end.

The illustration doesn't show clearly where the other five roof bricks sit. I recorded three on the Technic plate (b81) and two on the side rows of b79. These placements are guesses. The part type and count of six are certain.

Step 30 (page 35): a red round 2x2 plate with axle hole (b92) goes on the front of the rocket, and four more red inverted curved 2x1 bricks (b93-b96) complete the curved roof. That makes ten curved bricks in total with the six from step 29.
Step 31: the rocket is turned over (rotate icon). A green 1x2 plate (b97), a white 2x4 wedge plate (b98) and a flat silver grille tile (b99) are added on the studs now facing up.
The pictures are too small to give stud-level joins for these pieces, so I recorded only rough contact edges to the nearest major plate. The grille tile is the fourth flat silver 2412b used.
The studded face shown after the turn-over doesn't match my earlier guess of what sits under the red 4x6 plate (b79), so the placements on this page are uncertain.

Step 32 (page 36): six white inverted 1x2 brackets (b100-b105, the whole stock of lego-99780) are pressed onto the studded face of the turned-over rocket. Three go along the front edge, with their side studs facing out. Three go along the back edge.
Which studs each bracket covers isn't legible at this size, so I gave the joins to the base plate b79 without ports. Their exact supporting pieces are uncertain.

Step 33 (page 37) fits out the rocket's cockpit area. A white 2x2 plate (b106), a white divider panel (b107) and a yellow seat (b109) go onto the studded face of the rocket. A yellow Technic brick (b108, the last of the three yellow ones) drops in at the front left, next to the first white bracket (b100).
All joins are given without ports because the small illustration doesn't show which studs are used. The seat and panel are assumed to sit on the main plate b79.
Step 34 (page 38): a light bluish gray 1x2-1x2 bracket (b110) is pressed onto the studs at the right (tail) end of the rocket, next to the white wedge plate (b98). It has side studs facing outward.
Which studs it uses isn't clear at this size, so I gave the join without ports. It is assumed to sit on the white wedge.

Step 35 (page 39): two red 2x2 plates (b111, b112) are stacked on the rocket's tail end, over the white wedge b98. Two flat silver cones (b113, b114) are fitted as rear nozzles. The bracket b110 has only one catalogue port for its side studs (stud.2), so both cones use that port, but they sit on its two side studs.
In sub-step 2 a Trans-Red round plate is added on top of each cone. The parts box lists 4x and the finished nozzles show two red rings each, so I recorded two stacked plates per cone (b115-b118).
The cones' catalogue entry has no stud port, so the plates are joined to the cones without a port. The red plates' exact studs are estimated.

Step 36 (page 40): on the stacked red 2x2 plates at the tail (b112), a light bluish gray handle plate (b119) takes the two studs on the cockpit side. A red 30° sloped brick (b120) takes the two studs on the rear side, next to the nozzles.
Which pair of studs each piece takes is estimated from the illustration.

Step 37 (page 41): the rocket is flipped upright and red curved shell pieces are added around it. Two long red curved 1x4 bricks (b121, b122, lego-10314) go along the sides over the white brackets. Four small red curved 1x2 bricks (b123-b126, lego-6091) fill in the ends and tail.
I matched the picture's '2x' piece to lego-10314 (long curved, no studs) and the '4x' piece to lego-6091. These are the only red curved parts left in the inventory that fit those counts.
The pictures don't show which studs each curved piece clutches, so joins are given without ports. The assignment of the four small pieces to specific neighbours is a guess.

Step 38 (page 42): twelve round 1x1 plates (six Trans-Dark Blue, six Trans-Green) are added to the outer side faces of the six white brackets (b100-b105), two per bracket, alternating blue and green. They form the rocket's row of portholes or lights.

The bracket's catalogue entry has one side port (anti-stud.2) standing for its two side positions, so both plates on a bracket use that port. The colour alternation is as drawn, but which of the two side positions gets which colour is arbitrary.

Step 39 (page 43): a black 3L axle pin with 2L axle (b141) is pushed into the pin hole of the yellow Technic brick (b108) at the rocket's nose. A trans-clear panel (b140) is added as the windscreen at the front of the cockpit. The last red 2x2 plate (b139) goes on the top rear.
The pictures don't show which studs the clear panel and red plate use, so those joins are given without ports. The panel is assumed to sit on b108 and the plate on the white plate b106.
The pin's free axle end sticks out the side of the nose, probably to connect to the ride mechanism later.

Step 40 (page 44) builds the rocket's nose cone as a separate sub-assembly. Sub-step 1: a dark blue round 2x2 jumper plate (b143) goes on the four studs of the dark blue 4x4x2 cone (b142). Sub-step 2: a trans-clear radar dish (b144) goes on the jumper plate's centre stud, then a flat silver round plate (b145) goes on top. Sub-step 3: a Trans-Red round plate (b146) goes on top.
The parts box shows small round pieces I could only match by colour. I took the first as the flat silver round plate (lego-6141) and the third as the last Trans-Red round plate.
The dish has no stud port in the catalogue, so b145 is joined to it without a port. The cone isn't attached to the rocket yet.

Step 41 (page 45): the nose cone sub-assembly from step 40 is attached to the front of the rocket. The axle end of the black axle pin (b141), which sticks out of the nose, goes into the cone's axle hole (b142). No new pieces.

Step 41 (page 46): the rocket's fins are added. A white tail shuttle (b149), the tall fin on top, goes on the red 2x2 plate at the rear (b139). Two dark blue flags (b147, b148) clip onto the handles of the handle plate (b119) at the tail, forming the side fins.
Both flags are shown clipping onto the bars of b119, so I used one clip port on each flag and clip.1 and clip.2 on the handle plate. Which flag takes which handle is arbitrary.
The first flag is already visible in place on the right side of the picture, and the second is shown with arrows.

Step 42 (page 47): the finished rocket is mounted on top of the ride base. The pin of the driving ring connector (b50) on the grey axle sticking up from the roof opening goes into one of the pin holes of the rocket's white Technic plate (b81). The rocket then turns freely on the crank mechanism. No new pieces.
The illustration only shows the rocket being lowered onto the base. I picked the middle pin hole (pin-hole.2) of b81 as the one used, and the link is recorded as a turning join.
The arrow on the page points at the nose cone's tip (the trans-red plate b146), probably showing the direction to hold the rocket, and adds no join.
Page 48 shows the completed model next to the minifigure. It has no building step, so nothing was added.
Page 49 shows how to use the finished model: turning the crank at the side makes the rocket rock back and forth. It has no building step, so nothing was added.
Page 52 is the back cover (starry background with the LEGO trademark notice). It has no building step, so nothing was added.
